title: Click torque wrench with hex bits, 5–70 N·m

sources.citation: game-design: a click-type torque wrench with a hex bit socket drives a lug's set screw and clicks at its setting, so it has drive and torque, with no conductor size limit (the torqueDriver kind: what matters is drive and torque, not the handle). The torque a lug needs comes from the device's own marking (NFPA 70-2023 Art. 110.14(D), cited by number), never from a torque table.

game-design: a 3/8 in square-drive click wrench set from 5 to 70 N·m, so one tool reaches both the 5 N·m breaker box lugs and the 31 N·m meter-base lugs (common 3/8 in click wrenches span roughly 5–60 to 20–100 N·m; common practice, not read from one product). Its ±4 % accuracy is game-design: a figure makers commonly state for click wrenches to ISO 6789-1 (cited by number); the standard's deviation table wasn't read and search summaries of it disagree (±3 % to ±6 %).
game-design: the kit's hex bit sockets fit hexagon-socket (Allen) lug screws (hex keys, ISO 2936, cited by number); bit sizes are names.
